title: PUCN Order — Docket 26-02035 (2026-07-09)

PROCEDURAL ORDER NO. 5

The presiding officer in these dockets makes the following findings and conclusions:

1. On March 2, 2026, Nevada Power Company d/b/a NV Energy (“Nevada Power”)
filed with the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada (“Commission”) an application, designated
as Docket No. 26-02035, for approval of fuel and purchased power expenses, to reset the
Temporary Renewable Energy Development (“TRED”) charge, reset all components of the
Renewable Energy Program Rate (“REPR”), reset the Base Energy Efficiency Program Rates
(“Base EEPR”), reset the Base Energy Efficiency Implementation Rates (“Base EEIR”), reset the

Energy Efficiency Program Amortization Rate (“Amortization EEPR”), reset the Energy

Docket Nos. 26-02035, 26-02036, & 26-02037 Page 2

Efficiency Implementation Amortization Rate (“Amortization EEIR”), and reset the Expanded
Solar Program Costs (“ESPC”) rate.

2. On March 2, 2026, Sierra Pacific Power Company d/b/a NV Energy (“Sierra,”
and, together with Nevada Power, “NV Energy’) filed with the Commission an application,
designated as Docket No. 26-02036, for approval of fuel and purchased power expenses, to reset
the TRED charge, reset all components of the REPR, reset the Base EEPR, reset the Base EEIR,
reset the Amortization EEPR, reset the Amortization EEIR, and reset the ESPC rate.

3. On March 2, 2026, Sierra filed with the Commission an application, designated as
Docket No. 26-02037, for approval of natural gas expenses and to set the Gas Energy Efficiency
Rate.

4. NV Energy filed the applications pursuant to the Nevada Revised Statutes
(NRS”) and the Nevada Administrative Code (“NAC”) Chapters 703 and 704, including, but
not limited to, NRS 704.110, 704.185, and 704.187.

5. The Regulatory Operations Staff of the Commission (“Staff”) participates as a
matter of right pursuant to NRS 703.301.

6. On March 10, 2026, the Nevada Bureau of Consumer Protection (“BCP”) filed
notices of intent to intervene in Docket Nos. 26-02035, 26-02036, and 26-02037.

7. On March 11, 2026, the Commission issued notices of application and prehearing
conference in Docket Nos. 26-02035, 26-02036, and 26-02037.

8. On April 1, 2026, US Silica, Heavenly Valley, Limited Partnership, Nevada
Cement Company, Premier Magnesia, LLC, Prime Healthcare Services—Reno, LLC d/b/a Saint
Mary’s Regional Medical Center, Inc., and Renown Health (collectively, “NNIEU”) filed a

petition for leave to intervene (“PLTT”’) in Docket No. 26-02036.

Docket Nos. 26-02035, 26-02036, & 26-02037 Page 3

9. On April 8, 2026, NNIEU filed errata to its PLTI in Docket No. 26-02036.

10. OnApril 15, 2026, the presiding officer held prehearing conferences in all three
dockets. NV Energy, NNIEU, BCP, and Staff (the “Parties”) made appearances. Consolidation
of the dockets, NNIEU’s PLTI, and a procedural schedule were discussed.

11. On April 20, 2026, the presiding officer issued Procedural Order No. 1 and an
order granting NNIEU’s PLTL

12. On May 8, 2026, the presiding officer issued Procedural Order No. 2.

13. On May 19, 2026, NV Energy filed comments in response to Procedural Order
No. 2.
14. On May 21, 2026, NV Energy filed amendments to its applications in Docket
Nos. 26-02035 and 26-02036

15. On May 28, 2026, the Commission issued the Notice of Consumer Session and

Notice of Hearing.

16. On May 29, 2026, BCP and Staff filed reply comments to NV Energy’s May 19,
2026, comments.

17. OnJune 5, 2026, NV Energy filed reply comments to the May 29, 2026,
comments.

18. On June 9, 2026, the presiding officer held a continued prehearing conference.
NV Energy, NNIEU, BCP, and Staff made appearances. NV Energy’s provision of notice for the
consumer session, concerns with NV Energy’s new Fusion accounting system, and the
procedural schedule were discussed.

19. On June 11, 2026, the presiding officer issued Procedural Order No. 3.

20. On June 22, 2026, the presiding officer issued Procedural Order No. 4.

Docket Nos. 26-02035, 26-02036, & 26-02037 Page 4

21. On July 2, 2026, the Commission issued an Amended Notice of Consumer

Session, which moved the date and location of the consumer session to accommodate the volume

of anticipated attendees.

A. Procedural Schedule

22. The parties to the proceeding requested that the presiding officer reschedule the

continued prehearing conference currently scheduled for Friday, July 10, 2026, at 10:00 a.m.
Consequently, the Friday, July 10, 2026, continued prehearing conference is cancelled.

The following procedural schedule is hereby established:

a. The presiding officer will hold a CONTINUED PREHARING
CONFERENCE in person and via Microsoft Teams on WEDNESDAY,

JULY 29, 2026, at 9:30 a.m.

23.

Therefore, it is ordered:

1. The procedural schedule set forth in paragraphs 22 and 23 are adopted.

By the Commission,
